findings.location: scripts/i06_backend_profile.py check_evidence, SC00/SC08 binding. It compares only backendProfile.profile, implementationId and componentKeys, and per component processLabel, executable and artifactDigest. Also vectors.json evidenceAccepted A02 and A05 (and evidenceNegative E70, E71); README decision 7 ('The evidence record names its W02a backend profile', 'as in W02a') and the F8/F11 dispositions; criteria.json SC00, SC08.
findings.finding: check_evidence never applies W02a's own backend rules, so the 'W02a backend' it binds to can be one that the adopted W02a contract refuses. Two of the seven accepted variants are such backends. I validated them with jsonschema against architecture/native-profile-v2/qualification.schema.json $defs.backendProfile. A05 (implementationId 'unit-distribution' with six componentKeys) and A02 (implementationId 'selected-distribution') both fail with 'is not valid under any of the given schemas'. The reason is that backendProfile.oneOf admits only unit-distribution with the fixed eight-key list; W02a's R58 refuses the six-key fixture. E70 and E71 also start from W02a-invalid backends, although they are still refused for their stated reasons. A02, the production positive, keeps the fixture's backendComponents unchanged and only renames the profile: same executables, same placeholder digests sha256:...b000-b007 (equality probe: True). A type sweep over the backend accepted 606 of 1341 substitutions, because cgroupPath, apiIdentities and filePaths are never examined. The README's 'as in W02a' holds for W02a's generic six-to-eight schema rule but not for its only adopted profile. The record also does not 'name' a backend: the binding is implementationId equality with whatever backend the caller passes. No SC00-SC15 rule is broken, and production still refuses the fixture identity, so P7(a) is not reopened.
findings.requiredChange: State the caller obligation in the check_evidence docstring, README decision 7 and SC00/SC08: the backend must be the backendProfile and backendComponents of a record that W02a's check_record accepted. Alternatively, apply W02a's backendProfile rule inside check_evidence: the fixture implementationId implies W02a's eight-key list, and any other implementationId needs a W02a profile alternative. Make A05 a non-fixture six-component profile marked as anticipating a W03-added W02a profile, and add the six-key unit-distribution backend as a negative. Label A02's backend the same way and give it non-fixture component digests.

findings.location: scripts/i06_backend_profile.py check_rbac_snapshot (the no-grant shortcut 'if not grants: continue' runs before the closure lookup); README 'Identity closure' F1_LOOPBACK bullet and F12 disposition; identity-closure.json User system:apiserver note; criteria.json IC03
findings.finding: IC03 refuses only policy-relevant grants bound to User system:apiserver. S32 (serviceaccounts create) is refused. These probes are ACCEPTED by check_rbac_snapshot: User system:apiserver with get and list on configmaps and secrets in kube-system, and with get on nodes/stats. The README ('IC03 refuses any RBAC rule bound to the name'; 'IC03 refuses any'), the closure note ('any RBAC grant bound to the name is refused') and IC03 ('no RBAC grant to the loopback user') therefore claim more than the model checks. Round-1 F12 asked for any RBAC rule on that name to be refused. Its kubelet-client half is met, because the PROFILE name is fixed to planeon:apiserver-kubelet-client. The impact is low: the accepted grants are non-policy, OR05 keeps token Secrets absent, and no credential carries that name.
findings.requiredChange: In check_rbac_snapshot, refuse any non-empty effectiveRules for User system:apiserver before the no-grant shortcut, and add a negative with a non-policy rule. Otherwise reword the README, the closure note and IC03 to 'no policy-relevant grant'.

findings.location: README 'Still open' (P7(b), P7(c) carried to W02a-F); scripts/i06_backend_profile.py check_evidence SC08; out of subject: architecture/native-profile-v2/status.json carriedFindings.P7 ('W02g and W03: ... type-name wording; nested backend cgroups')
findings.finding: W02a's frozen status record still assigns all of P7 to 'W02g and W03', while W02g carries P7(b) and P7(c) back to W02a-F. The carry is explicit and names its successor, but only this README records the chain. W02g now holds the W02a backend rows, yet check_evidence ACCEPTS a SCHEDULER cgroupPath nested under the KUBELET cgroupPath and a cgroupPath shared by two components. The I06 evidence path could refuse P7(c) itself, as it does for P7(a).
findings.requiredChange: Record the P7(b) and P7(c) carry to W02a-F in the W02g status record that adoption writes. Optionally refuse nested or equal backend cgroupPath values under SC08, with a negative.

findings.location: scripts/i06_backend_profile.py SEALED_FILES / CONDITIONAL_SEALED_FILES; README decision 8 ('the PKI trust bundles (client CA and service-account verification keys)'); criteria.json SC12
findings.finding:
The sealed vocabulary names categories, not files. The parenthetical can be read as covering only the apiserver's client CA, so some files that decide authority stay implicit:
- The kubelet's client CA bundle is reloaded dynamically (cmd/kubelet/app/auth.go:72-116). A CA added to it can mint a certificate with group system:masters that the kubelet's Webhook SubjectAccessReview allows, which gives exec on every pod.
- The kubelet --config-dir drop-in directory can set staticPodURL at the next kubelet start (cmd/kubelet/app/options/options.go:282, cmd/kubelet/app/server.go:223-232).
- The apiserver's --egress-selector-config-file is another such file.
The record also has no field for --kubelet-certificate-authority. Without it, the apiserver's kubelet transport is Insecure (pkg/kubelet/client/kubelet_client.go:114-129). Spec P5/2.6 and W02e still seal host files, so this is a mapping obligation, not an open path.
findings.requiredChange: Enumerate PKI_TRUST_BUNDLES: the apiserver client CA, the kubelet client CA, the service-account verification keys, and the kubelet serving CA if one is used. State that KUBELET_CONFIG includes --config-dir drop-ins, and that APISERVER_FLAGS covers every file a sealed flag references. Carry the file-level mapping and the apiserver-to-kubelet serving-certificate verification to W02e/W03.

findings.location: criteria.json SC13, SC14; check_evidence SC14 (record['kubernetesVersion'] == 'v1.37.1'); README 'Baseline and sources' and decision 1; spec 2.5 last sentence
findings.finding: The inventory and closure hold only for unmodified upstream v1.37.1 sources. SC13/SC14 do not require component binaries to be upstream builds, and they do not define kubernetesVersion as the components' reported gitVersion. A vendor-patched apiserver or controller-manager could add in-process writers that run as the loopback system:masters identity and are invisible to IC, although spec 2.5 requires distribution additions to be listed or disabled. The exact string match refuses truthful vendor suffixes, but only if the field is defined as the reported gitVersion.
findings.requiredChange: Define kubernetesVersion as the gitVersion every Kubernetes component reports, with no vendor suffix. Require components built from the unmodified v1.37.1 tag, or a vendor patch set reviewed against the inventory, or carry this explicitly to W03.

findings.location: scripts/i06_backend_profile.py WORKLOAD_RESOURCES / PROTECTED_NAMESPACES and the category tables; README 'Policy-relevant grants' (WORKLOAD rationale) and 'Still open' (W02f)
findings.finding:
WORKLOAD is classified only at cluster scope and in kube-system, on a service-account rationale. Two host-access paths stay unclassified and are accepted by check_rbac_snapshot.
(1) An unknown User with pods create in 'default'; kube-public and kube-node-lease work the same way. PodSecurity's built-in default for unlabeled namespaces is enforce=privileged (staging/src/k8s.io/pod-security-admission/admission/api/v1/defaults.go:28-37), and the writer controls labels only in the qualification namespace. Whether a privileged or hostPath pod can run there therefore depends on the sealed admission configuration and on W02f.
(2) An unknown User with persistentvolumes create. PodSecurity checks pod volume types, not the source of a bound PV, so a hostPath PV reaches the host from any namespace where the holder can create pods and claims.
Both need a binding that only TCB can create, and SELinux (W02e) remains the barrier to credential files. This is a gap in defence-in-depth detection, not an open path.
findings.requiredChange: Carry to W02f: PodSecurity defaults of at least baseline (restricted where possible) for every namespace in the sealed admission configuration, and refusal of hostPath or local PersistentVolumes. Carry to W02e: container domains cannot read component credentials. Alternatively, classify as WORKLOAD both pod creation in any namespace other than the qualification namespace and persistentvolumes create.

F1.note: check_closure pins the five PROFILE identities: closed key set, holder and presence, and exact grants (writer_grants(), derive_grants(system:kubelet-api-admin), [] for the others). The writer's resourceNames must be exactly the two roles. The three component users and closure accounts in accounts - dormant are pinned too. C05-C17 replay exactly and cover every round-1 probe shape. My extra probes were all refused: Group-kind writer, holder or presence flips, extra Group via BOOTSTRAP, SA outside kube-system, unknown derivation, reordered resourceNames, writer verb '*', and a User named like an SA. Only 'note' and the unused 'scopes' accept arbitrary values.

F2.note: serviceAccountTokens records signingEndpoint (must be null), signingKeyReaders ([APISERVER]), verificationKeys (int, exactly 1), verificationKeyIsSigningPublicKey (true), issuers (exactly one) and lookup (true). E48-E52 are refused, and the type probes True, 0, '' and 1 are refused. Upstream semantics verified: options.go:205-209,305-345 (the endpoint is mutually exclusive with the key files and supplies its own public keys); kube_features.go:1612-1616 (GA, locked); authentication.go:225 (lookup default true), 282-283 (key file or endpoint required), 430-435 and 621-642 (several files and several keys).

F3.note: Any staticPodURL other than null, or staticPodURLHeader other than {}, is refused (E53, E54; '' and None probes refused). In v1.37.1 the only pod sources are file, URL and apiserver (pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go:373-404; v1beta1 types.go:152-159).

F4.note: Absent controller accounts are limited to their bootstrap grants and closure entry (S28-S30). Probes refused: token create on the absent certificate-controller; pods/exec on an absent non-controller kube-system SA and on an absent SA outside kube-system (IC01). An absent namespace-controller carrying only its own grants is accepted, as intended.

F5.note: featureGates is keyed exactly by the gated components present and each must be {}. emulatedVersion and minCompatibilityVersion must be null and runtimeConfig must be {} (E27, E57-E59; '1.37' and missing-component probes refused). get on pods/exec and pods/attach is SPECIAL (S31). A single emulatedVersion field stands for all three components that register the flag: apiserver (server_run_options.go:401), controller-manager (options.go:315) and scheduler (options.go:217). 'Must stay unset' is therefore a whole-cluster claim, which is acceptable.

F6.note: The sealed set must equal the profile's set exactly. It includes PKI_TRUST_BUNDLES, CONTAINER_RUNTIME_CONFIG and CNI_CONFIG, plus AUTHENTICATION_CONFIG, AUDIT_CONFIG, ADMISSION_MANIFESTS and the agent and proxy configuration when used (E33, E37, E47, E63-E66, A01, A06, A07). An unknown token and a stale proxy configuration are refused. The file-level mapping residual is N4.

F7.note: _path refuses '.', '..', empty segments, a trailing '/' and relative paths. Executables and artifactDigests must be pairwise distinct. W02a binds artifactDigest to the executable file's sha256 (native_qualification_v2.py _Owners.own), so symlinks, hard links and copies collide (E38, E55, E56 and probes). Decision 7 now says that a multi-call binary with modified content is still accepted.

F8.note: The evidence is bound to its W02a profile by implementationId under W02a's pattern. Production refuses the fixture implementationId and distribution name (E35, E36, E60-E62). A02 uses a non-fixture identity. P7(b) and P7(c) are explicitly carried to W02a-F. The binding's weakness and A02's reuse of fixture components are N1.

F9.note: The bootstrap-roles reason and the README now match storage_rbac.go:197-202,257,274,306,322, reconciliation/namespace.go:28-45 and policy.go:761-779. The F1_LOOPBACK text separates API writers from in-process storage writers, and OR07 is added.

F10.note: nodes/log and nodes/checkpoint are SPECIAL with KUBELET_VERBS (S33, S34; verified in kubelet auth.go:83-156 and server.go:693-700,730-758). VAP paramKind is carried to W02f; upstream additionally requires get on the paramKind (validatingadmissionpolicy/authz.go:57-102). The audit policy is sealed when used, and keeping token and secret bodies out of logs is carried to W02e.

F11.note: Integer and boolean checks are strict (E67-E69); a sweep of 2780 type substitutions on the evidence record accepted only 11, all semantically valid. SC08 takes the component set from W02a componentKeys, with six required (A05, E70, E71). SC14 is exactly v1.37.1 (E41). A05's backend is W02a-invalid: see N1.

F12.note: The closure gives User system:apiserver no grant, and the kubelet client is fixed to planeon:apiserver-kubelet-client. However, only policy-relevant grants to system:apiserver are refused. Non-policy rules are accepted (get and list on secrets and configmaps in kube-system, get on nodes/stats), contrary to the README disposition 'IC03 refuses any' (N2).

questionAnswers.Q1: F1-F11 are CLOSED and F12 is PARTIAL (see openItemStatus). Each README disposition is present in the round-2 bytes, and the vectors it cites replay exactly. The exception is F12: 'IC03 refuses any' holds only for policy-relevant grants (N2). F8 and F11 are closed as specified, but the accepted variants they cite (A02, A05) use backends that the adopted W02a schema refuses (N1).
questionAnswers.Q3:
Accurate for v1.37.1.

Tag and files. refs/tags/v1.37.1 is tag object d2b770f4, which points to commit f78e7223. Twenty files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at the tag are byte-identical to the author's tree, and the six fixture digests equal the recorded ones.

Independent derivations:
- My own resolver re-derives the 56 bootstrap subjects with identical rules and order.
- system:kubelet-api-admin is unbound, and its four rules equal referencedRoles.
- The 49 KCM registrations match the inventory in name and order.

Round-2 facts verified:
- The signing endpoint is mutually exclusive with the key files and supplies its own public keys (options.go:205-209,305-345).
- ExternalServiceAccountTokenSigner is GA and locked since 1.36 (kube_features.go:1612-1616).
- The key-file flag accepts several files and several keys (authentication.go:430-435,621-642); lookup defaults to true (authentication.go:225).
- staticPodURL and its header exist (types.go:152-159); file, URL and apiserver are the only pod sources (kubelet.go:373-404).
- The emulation floor is the binary version minus 3, i.e. 1.34 (util/compatibility/version.go:43-50). The emulation flags are registered by the apiserver, controller-manager and scheduler.
- Kubelet API mapping: /logs maps to log (system log handler, GET only); /checkpoint maps to checkpoint (POST; ContainerCheckpoint beta, default on since 1.30); everything else defaults to proxy, and fine-grained pods, healthz and configz fall back to proxy (auth.go:83-156; server.go:693-700,730-758).
- Feature gates: AuthorizePodWebsocketUpgradeCreatePermission beta default on since 1.35; ConstrainedImpersonation beta since 1.36; KubeletFineGrainedAuthz GA locked since 1.36; ManifestBasedAdmissionControlConfig beta default on in 1.37; StorageVersionMigrator GA in 1.37.
- The admission allowlist (27) is the plugins.go default-on set minus the three forbidden plugins, plus NodeRestriction and four others.
- The default authorization mode is AlwaysAllow (authorization.go:91).

Wording nits: the README calls the GC and namespace-controller grants 'wildcard verbs', but they are wildcard resources with explicit verbs; AlwaysPullImages mutates pods rather than only restricting them.
questionAnswers.Q5:
Mostly sound.
- PROFILE pinning holds. My probes of the closed key set, holder and presence, exact sorted grants, derivation, Group kind and resourceNames were all refused, and a sweep of 7703 substitutions accepted changes only to 'note' and the unused 'scopes'.
- The dormant rule holds.
- Canonical, distinct executables hold.
- The exact sealed set holds.
- The strict type checks hold: of 2780 substitutions on the evidence record only 11 semantically valid values were accepted, and no exception escaped explain().
- The W02a binding is weak. It covers three profile fields and four component fields, and it accepts backends that the adopted W02a schema refuses: A05, A02, and 606 of 1341 backend substitutions (N1).
- check_inventory compares against the author's facts, which I checked against upstream separately.
- The snapshot model fails safe for '*'-verb allowances: a narrower explicit-verb rule for the kubelet client would be refused, which is acceptable.

reviewLimit: This review is static reading of the author-fetched v1.37.1 tree, cross-checked against 20 raw upstream files and the tag ref. Nothing was run against a cluster, no Go code was built or executed, and no SELinux policy was analysed (that is W02e). The probes test the reference model's data checks, not a real observer, a distribution or W02a's model; W02a validity was checked only with jsonschema against the adopted schema's backend definitions. The packet's out-of-subject edits (validators, tests, catalog, authority JSON and packet YAML) were not reviewed; the packet YAML and the authority JSON were only glanced at, read-only, for carry context. Git use was limited to read-only status and rev-parse. No repository file was modified. Scratch scripts and fetched upstream copies live only in scratchpad/reviewer-w02g-r2/. A PASS is not a selected distribution, an observed cluster, an installed profile or authorization to install anything. The MINOR and NOTE findings are carried forward, not waived.
